findings.note: Dead assertion at internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:139-141: `if strings.Contains(user, "{{") && kind == KindMatch && mode.name == "plain" && !strings.Contains(user, "in {{loop}}") { t.Fatal("values are inserted verbatim, never rescanned") }`. The guard and the body condition are mutually exclusive. Every `{{` in the templates unescapes to a single `{` (prompts.go:213-247), so the only `{{` that can reach the rendered match/plain output is the verbatim golden value "off-by-one in {{loop}}" - confirmed by counting: testdata/prompts/match.plain.golden contains exactly one `{{`, on line 7, inside that value. Therefore strings.Contains(user, "{{") is true precisely when strings.Contains(user, "in {{loop}}") is also true, and the t.Fatal is unreachable. If format() ever did rescan inserted values the `{{` would disappear from the output, the guard would go false, and this check would pass silently. The property it names is genuinely covered elsewhere - the format("{{x}} {v} }}", {"v": "{v}"}) case at line 165 and the pinned goldens - so the fix is to delete the dead check or replace it with a direct equality on the rendered slot.

evidence.note: The guard strings.Contains(user, "{{") is true only in the case the body condition rules out, so t.Fatal is unreachable.
grep -o '{{' match.plain.golden returns exactly one hit, the verbatim golden comment - no template-origin {{ survives rendering.
format("{{x}} {v} }}", {"v": "{v}"}) == "{x} {v} }" is the check that really pins no-rescan.

findings.note: FSM_JUDGE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 skips the checks that were written to be golden-independent. The update branch at internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:115-120 ends in `continue`, which jumps past the block introduced at line 127 as 'authority checks independent of the golden' (fenced values must be JSON-encoded, calibration is never fenced, match is never fenced, {{ }} unescapes). Regeneration is exactly the moment those invariants matter, since a drifted rendering is about to be written into the goldens and become the new baseline. Running them before the write - or writing first and falling through instead of continuing - would close the hole.

evidence.note: continue in the update branch skips the rest of the mode loop body.
The comment 'authority checks independent of the golden' introduces checks that only run when not updating.

findings.note: TestJ1Provenance's sibling layer is non-hermetic in ways that can fail on state outside the repository. siblingSource stats $HOME/Developer/harnesseval by path only (internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:74) - any directory with that name qualifies - and then hard-fails, not skips, when `git show 19ff9a8:...` cannot read the pinned object (line 84), so a shallow clone, a fork without that commit, or an unrelated directory of the same name breaks the unit suite. os.UserHomeDir's error is dropped at line 71, which would make repo a relative path. And line 92 slices with strings.Index(rest, '"""') without checking for -1, so a literal whose closing delimiter moved panics instead of reporting drift. The sha256 header pin checked at line 61 already gives the provenance guarantee without any of this, so the sibling layer is additive; hardening it (or gating it behind an opt-in env var) costs nothing.

evidence.note: os.Stat on $HOME/Developer/harnesseval decides whether the layer runs, on path alone.
t.Fatalf when the pinned object is unreadable, so an unrelated local repo state fails the suite.
rest[:strings.Index(rest, `\"\"\"`)] panics on a missing closing delimiter.
